notes: §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SR4 has two bars. The GLOBAL half ("The same data-name must not be used as the name of an item possessing the global attribute and as the name of any other data item described in the program") is DataBinder.ScreenGlobalNameUniqueness (CheckGlobalNameUniquenessPass), COBOL6862 with a 1985 message arm; the EXTERNAL half ("the same data-name must not be used as the name of an external record and as the name of any other external data item described in any program contained within or containing the program") is ExternalRecordNameRules.Check, COBOL7282 (kb/Work PB5427). ADJUDICATED by kb/Work PB5629 (2026-11-16): the item that POSSESSES the global attribute is the entry that carries the GLOBAL clause (or whose FD does), the record; the data-names subordinate to it are global NAMES (§1985:X.4.6.4 GR1, a matter of scope) told apart by qualification (§1985:X.1.3.8.2 GR1: "the normal rules for qualification and any other rules for uniqueness of reference are applied until one or more objects is identified"), as §1985:X.4.6.4 GR3 ("it is only the subject of that REDEFINES clause which possesses the global attribute") and §1985:X.1.3.8.3 ("a data item possessing the global attribute includes a table") keep the attribute apart from the global name. So the screen refuses a GLOBAL record's own name reused by another item (conformance:cases/IV.4.3.8@1985-Uniqueness-of-Reference/1985-SR-IV_4_3_8_1-4) and two GLOBAL records of one name (X.4.6.3 SR2), and leaves same-named subordinates to qualification (conformance:pb5629_global_subordinate_names_told_apart_by_qualification, accepted at 85: two X under one GLOBAL record, output 12 then 123); an unqualified reference to such a pair is COBOL1639 at the reference (conformance:negative/pb1047-two-globals-one-element-ambiguous at 85). Reading A (every subordinate possesses the attribute) of the earlier PB5150 adjudication is reversed. The EXTERNAL half holds on every probe (COBOL7282 for r3-ext-bad, s4-x-same, s4-x-fd; siblings, a non-external local item and two programs sharing the record compile and run).

next.reason: 1985 bars reusing an external record's data-name for another external item 'described in any program contained within or containing the program which describes that external data record'. 2023 states the bar in the uncataloged prose of §2023:8.4.2.1, 'as the name of any other external data item described in the run unit'. The scope widened from the containment nest to the whole run unit, which covers separately compiled programs: stricter. The global-name half is unchanged ('in the source element that describes that global data item'). The qualification formats map to §2023:8.4.2.2.2, which drops the cd-name qualifier (communication removed) and adds the report-name qualifier and further formats. Catalog defect: the §2023:8.4.2.1 paragraph that carries the external/global bar has no rule id, so 'to' cannot name it.
